neighbours.label: the word right after a verb of motion, describing how it goes: 'moved as fast', 'slinked over', 'walked on as though', 'torn asunder'
fire: The company has moved as quickly as the market has grown.
The kingdom was torn asunder by greed.
Like a beaten puppy he slunk over to the door.
She walked on as though nothing had happened.
He crept over to the window.
They marched on as if the war had ended.
The car sped through the gate.
The cat tiptoed over to the bowl.
quiet: The company has been sold since the market has grown.
The kingdom was ruled by a cruel queen.
Like a good puppy he sat next to the door.
She stayed home because nothing had happened.
He stood next to the window.
They rested at home when the war had ended.
The car stopped near the gate.
The cat ate from the bowl.

short: after a motion verb: as / over
notes: The + pole of this neuron fires on verbs of sound and movement ('creaked', 'clicked', 'sobbed').
